name: Somchai
livingSituation: Lives alone in a 1-bedroom condo on the 4th floor in Nonthaburi. Son Pete works in Chiang Mai and visits once or twice a month. Nearest neighbor is an elderly couple named Prasert and Noi two doors down.
caregiverNotes: Somchai tends to downplay discomfort — if he says he is fine, ask once more gently. He missed his Amlodipine on Monday because he woke up late and skipped breakfast. His knees have been stiff this week from the rain. He has not heard from Pete in 4 days and mentioned it casually but his voice was noticeably flat. Bring up his chili peppers or his stamp collection — both topics make him light up immediately.

healthConditions.notes: Managed with Amlodipine 5mg every morning. Somchai tends to forget when he skips breakfast. Emotional stress and loneliness can raise blood pressure. If he mentions headache and dizziness at the same time, escalate to Level 3 immediately.

Gets worse in rainy or cold weather. Somchai refuses to admit how much it hurts — he will say the knees are fine when they are clearly not. Ask directly on rainy days. Remind him not to stand too long when gardening on the balcony.

medications.name: Amlodipine
medications.notes: Once daily in the morning. Does not require food. If he skips, flag to Pete immediately. Ask gently — do not alarm him.

medications.name: Glucosamine
medications.notes: Must be taken with breakfast. Always ask if he has eaten first before checking on this medication. He skipped it Monday because he had no appetite.

dailySchedule.morningRoutine: Makes coffee, sits on the balcony, checks on chili pepper plants
dailySchedule.afternoonActivity: Watches old Muay Thai fights on YouTube from 15:00, tends to balcony garden 16:00
dailySchedule.eveningRoutine: Watches evening news at 19:00, sorts his stamp collection at 20:00

hobbies: Growing chili peppers on his balcony — currently has 6 pots, very proud of a Prik Kee Noo plant that is finally turning red after 3 weeks
Watching classic Muay Thai fights on YouTube — favorite era is the 1980s, favorite fighter is Samart Payakaroon
Collecting vintage Thai postage stamps — has been collecting for 30 years, most prized stamp is a 1967 SEAP Games commemorative issue

personality.temperament: Warm and talkative once comfortable, but puts up a tough front at first. Tends to be slightly dramatic about small things and completely stoic about serious things. Loves to make people laugh.
personality.communicationStyle: Direct but indirect about pain — will joke about something that is actually bothering him. Listen between the lines.
sensitivities: Does not want Pete to worry or feel guilty about working far away
Gets quietly lonely in the evenings after 20:00 when the house is too quiet
Proud man — dislikes being reminded he is getting older
Hates being told what to do — frame everything as a suggestion, never a command
brightensWhen: Talking about his Prik Kee Noo chili pepper finally turning red
Showing off knowledge about rare Thai stamps
Telling stories about Pete as a child

emergencyContact.name: Pete
emergencyContact.relationship: Son — Primary caregiver and family contact
emergencyContact.location: Chiang Mai — approximately 700km away, flies down once or twice a month
emergencyContact.alertThreshold: medium — notify for loneliness signals, missed medications, low mood lasting more than one session
emergencyContact.preferredAlertMethod: SMS first, then call if no response within 15 minutes

sessionContext.lastSessionSummary: Somchai made several jokes but his answers were shorter than usual. Mentioned Pete had not called in a few days and immediately said it was fine. Mood lifted briefly when he talked about his chili pepper almost being ready. Did not complain about knees but moved around stiffly during the session.
caregiverNotes: Skipped Amlodipine on Monday — woke up late and skipped breakfast entirely.
Knees are stiff this week from the rainy season but he will not admit it.
Mentioned Pete casually but his voice dropped — classic Somchai sign that he misses him.
Bring up the chili pepper turning red — he almost smiled talking about it last time.
